fields.title: Interface for a slow response
fields.keyTakeaway: Streaming, a filled pause before the first token, and output starting with useful info turn an eight-second response into an acceptable one without a single millisecond of acceleration.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: The response takes eight seconds. How to build a screen so this works?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: AI features are almost always slower than what users are accustomed to. A product that hasn't designed the waiting experience loses people on a feature that objectively works.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: Five techniques specific to generative responses.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: **Streaming is mandatory** where the response is longer than a couple of sentences. Lack of streaming is the most common mistake of early AI feature versions.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: **Show what is happening before the first token.** TTFT is a pause where nothing is printed. Filled with an indicator and text: "searching for matching items".
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: **Show intermediate steps** if there are several. "Found 12 items → checking availability → assembling set". Turns eight seconds of waiting into watching work happen.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: **Provide an ability to interrupt.** A "stop" button on long generation. Cheap, strongly reduces annoyance.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: **Structure output so useful info appears first.** If the response starts with a preamble, the person reads useless info. The instruction should require jumping straight to the point—this is a product requirement for format.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: Separately — **what to do with an error in the middle.** The response started and cut off. The product must decide: show partial, retry entirely, show error. Usually the right thing is to retry, but not silently.
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: *0–1.1 s:* "Looking at what you usually buy". *1.1–3 s:* first items appear as they generate. *3–7.8 s:* set is supplemented, sum counter updates. *All the time:* "Stop" button.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: The instruction requires starting with items rather than an explanation. The first version started with the phrase "I have picked a weekly set for you taking into account your previous purchases"—22 tokens of useless text before the first item, meaning an extra 250 milliseconds before useful info.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: Generation cutoff: assembled part is shown plus "failed to finish assembling" and a retry button. A partial set is useful in its own right.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: We measured the effect of streaming: without it, drop-off on this feature was 34%, with streaming—11%. Time did not change.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Streaming complicates validation: checking the response as a whole is only possible when it's ready. For scenarios with strict checking, streaming may be inapplicable, and then an honest indicator is needed.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Streaming, a filled pause before the first token, and output starting with useful info turn an eight-second response into an acceptable one without a single millisecond of acceleration.
